title: Endpoint & model SLOs + error-budget policy, multi-region failover, circuit breakers, and load-shedding
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Background:
Redwood must standardize how we measure and enforce reliability for public endpoints and model variants. Recent incidents (INC-2026-02: regional networking flaps; INC-2026-03: kv-cache stampede) exposed gaps: (1) inconsistent SLI definitions across routes, (2) no unified error budget policy tying rollouts to failover, and (3) ad-hoc circuit-breaker settings that caused either over-aggressive shedding or slow degradation.

Goal:
- Define canonical SLIs per endpoint and per model variant (hosted API routes, streaming vs non-streaming, embeddings, and reranking).
- Set SLOs and error budgets with clear burn policies and automated responses (rate-limit tighten, alpha fallback to cheaper model, regional failover).
- Publish circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding rules with safe defaults and per-customer override hooks for Dedicated/Private.
- Produce runbooks, dashboards, and alerting rules so on-call can execute failovers and undeploy problematic model variants safely.

Scope (this ticket):
- Produce the SLI -> SLO mapping document for top 12 endpoints and top 6 model families served in production.
- Define error budget burn actions (policy table) and automated enforcement steps (scripts/playbooks).
- Policy for multi-region failover order and automated rollback triggers tied to error budget exhaustion.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds (5xx rate, p95 latency, token-limited queue depth) and suggested backoffs.
- Load-shedding priorities by customer tier and endpoint type.
- Deliverables: SLO spec doc (Confluence), patch to alerting rules (Grafana/Prometheus), one infra PR for circuit-breaker config defaults, and runbook draft.

Proposed SLI definitions (examples):
- API.text.generate (non-streaming):
  - Success SLI: fraction of requests producing a 2xx/stream-close within 60s and no model-returned "error" envelope.
  - Latency SLI: p95 server-side response time for token-generation start-to-end (ms).
  - Quality SLI: fraction of requests with hallucination score < threshold on sampling evals (for runtime alerts, will be a lower-frequency metric).
- API.chat.stream (streaming):
  - Success SLI: fraction of streams that reach final-token-with-status=complete within 120s and without mid-stream error frames.
  - Latency SLI: 95th percentile first-token latency + per-token generation p95.
- Embeddings.generate:
  - Success SLI: 2xx responses within 10s and vector normalization constraints met.

SLO targets and windows (proposal):
- Critical endpoints (text.generate, chat.stream): 99.95% success over 30d window, p95 latency < X ms (X depends on model size: e.g., small=200ms, medium=450ms, large=900ms).
- Embeddings: 99.9% success over 30d.
- Reranking: 99.5% over 30d.
- Reserved/enterprise routes may have stricter SLOs pinned per contract and will be recorded as overrides.

Error budget policy (automated + human):
- Error budget defined as 1 - SLO over rolling 30 days. For a 99.95% SLO, budget = 0.05% of requests.
- Burn rate windows: instant (5m), short (1h), medium (24h), long (30d).
- Automated actions by burn rate severity:
  - Burn rate < 5x: notify on-call, add to daily ops queue.
  - 5x <= burn rate < 20x: tighten rate-limits for unverified clients by 30%, enable degraded model fallback for non-enterprise tier, create priority incident page.
  - burn rate >= 20x or remaining budget < 10%: trigger circuit-breaker on offending model/route, initiate multi-region failover according to policy, and engage SRE pager (P0).
- Failed rollouts: if new model variant rollout causes error budget burn > 10% in 1h, automatic rollback to previous version and block re-rollout until postmortem is completed.

Circuit-breaker and load-shedding defaults (proposal):
- Metrics considered: 5xx rate (client and server separate), p95 latency, queued requests > threshold, kv-cache miss amplification, per-instance CPU/gpu saturation.
- Default breakers per route/model:
  - 5xx rate > 0.5% sustained over 5m -> open breaker for that model-variant for 1m then probe.
  - p95 latency > SLO-latency * 2 for 10m -> open breaker and shift 30% of traffic to fallback model.
  - Queue depth > 2000 requests (aggregated per region) -> start shedding 20% of lowest-priority traffic, escalate every 30s until under threshold.
- Circuit state machine: CLOSED -> PROBING (10% traffic) -> HALF_OPEN (30% traffic) -> CLOSED; backoff doubles on repeated failures.
- Per-customer overrides: Dedicated customers may set custom breaker thresholds within approved safety bounds; Private deployments default to their local config.

Multi-region failover policy (sequence):
1. Local region degradation detected -> attempt local load-shedding and scaling for 2m.
2. If not recovered and error budget burning at >=5x -> route non-enterprise traffic to secondary region(s) (order: US-West -> US-East -> EU-West) based on geo proximity and latency impact.
3. If global degradation or connectivity issues across multiple regions -> switch to minimal-safe-serving mode: reduce max tokens per request (configurable), enforce strict rate limits, and serve only critical endpoints.
4. Failback policy: once SLI metrics return within 80% of SLO for 30m with stable CPU/GPU utilization, gradually shift traffic back over 15m with canary probes.

Observability, alerts and dashboards:
- Dashboards: per-model SLI canvas with success rate, latency percentiles, burn rate meter, and top contributing error codes.
- Alerts: two tiers: "burn-warning" (pager-team optional, slack alert) and "burn-critical" (pager). Alert conditions will be encoded in Prometheus as rules using rolling windows.
- Suggested queries included below (PromQL examples).

Runbooks and playbooks:
- Short runbook for on-call: detect, isolate (model vs infra vs network), degrade safely (circuit-breaker and load-shed steps), failover (region order), rollback deployment, and communicate.
- Post-incident: incident owner to publish timeline and update SLO mapping if SLI was insufficient.

Trade-offs and decisions to document:
- Aggressive shedding prevents widespread latency but increases false negatives for long-running legitimate requests (trade-off between availability and UX).
- Using quality-based SLI is useful but high-cardinality and noisy; treat as secondary signal.
- Multi-region failover increases costs and may expose data residency concerns; require an allowlist per customer.

Next steps / Deliverables by 2026-04-01:
- Confluence SLO spec (this ticket) published and reviewed by PM and Design.
- PR: infra defaults for circuit-breaker config (k8s ConfigMap + runtime flags) -> target: eng/reliability#314.
- Grafana/Prometheus rule updates PR to monitoring repo -> target: monitoring#892.
- Draft runbook (shared drive link) and tabletop with on-call simulated failover.

Monitoring rules (Prometheus) implement burn-rate alerts and at least two circuit-breaker alerts in monitoring repo PR
Infra PR adds circuit-breaker defaults and a runtime flag for per-tenant overrides
Runbook draft exists and tabletop performed with notes and action items
Post-deployment smoke tests and canary configured to auto-rollback on >10% error-budget burn in 1h
telemetry_queries: SQL (analytics): SELECT model_variant, count(*) as requests, SUM(case when status >= 500 then 1 else 0 end) as errors FROM request_logs WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '1 day' GROUP BY model_variant ORDER BY errors DESC LIMIT 20
